name: open_1
prose: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv_open("nonexisting", "foobar"). If the call returned (iconv_t)-1 and errno equals EINVAL it returns 0. In every other outcome it calls iconv_close on the returned descriptor (including a (iconv_t)-1 result with a different errno) and returns 1.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:41-55; first reviewer-style claims (formal weaker) not applicable, contract left empty. Prose checked against lines 46-54

name: open_2
prose: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv_open("ASCII", "UTF8") in a loop of at most 1025 iterations, storing each descriptor in a local array. On the first call that returns (iconv_t)-1 it sets the result to 0 if errno is ENFILE or EMFILE (the result stays 1 for any other errno), stores NULL in that slot and stops. It then calls iconv_close on slots i down to 1, where i is the failed index or 1024 if no call failed; slot 0 is never closed, and a NULL slot is passed to iconv_close when a failure occurred at index 1 or later. Returns 1 if all 1025 opens succeeded, 0 only in the ENFILE/EMFILE case.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:62-84; loop 71-79, close loop 81-82, return 83. Reviewer claim (non-ENFILE failure returns 1) is right and the prose states it

name: close_1
prose: Calls iconv_close on the invalid descriptor (iconv_t)-1. If it returns -1 the condition assigns EBADF to errno (the test uses '=' not '==', so the assignment is evaluated only when the call returned -1) and the function returns 0; if iconv_close returns anything other than -1 the function returns 1 and errno is not assigned.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:90-96, return expression at line 95 uses (errno = EBADF), an assignment

name: conv_ebadf
prose: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv on the descriptor (iconv_t)-1 with NULL input and output pointers and zero byte counts. Returns 0 when iconv returned (size_t)-1 with errno equal to EBADF, and 1 otherwise.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:98-105

name: conv_2big
prose: Opens an "ASCII" to "ASCII" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv with a 16-byte input and an 8-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when the input pointer advanced by 8 bytes, inbytesleft is 8, outbytesleft is 0, the output pointer advanced by 8 bytes, errno is E2BIG and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is not closed on any path, and the input buffer is uninitialised.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:128-165; return at 159-164; no iconv_close call in the function

name: conv_einval
prose: Opens a "UTF-32" from "BIG5" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv on a 2-byte input (the uint16_t value 0xEA42) with a 16-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when the input pointer advanced by 1 byte, inbytesleft is 1, outbytesleft is 8, the output pointer advanced by 8 bytes, errno is EINVAL and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is never closed.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:167-203; conditions at 198-203. Reviewer 'formal weaker' is moot (no contract)

name: conv_eilseq
prose: Opens a "Latin2" from "UTF-16LE" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv with the pointer to a 2-byte buffer holding the uint16_t 0x8AC0 but with inbytesleft set to 4, so iconv is told there are two more bytes than the buffer holds, and with a 16-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when no input was consumed (pointer offset 0, inbytesleft 4), nothing was produced (outbytesleft 16, pointer offset 0), errno is EILSEQ and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is not closed.
note: tools/test/iconv/posix/posix.c:206-240; inbytesleft = 4 at line ~231 with a 1-element uint16_t buffer. Reviewer claim (4 bytes from a 2-byte buffer) is right; prose now states it and no longer calls the value invalid

name: random_int
prose: Returns arc4random() % (ma - mi + 1) + mi. arc4random() returns an unsigned 32-bit value and the divisor (int ma - mi + 1) is converted to unsigned for the modulo, so the remainder is non-negative. When mi <= ma and ma - mi + 1 does not overflow int, the remainder is in [0, ma - mi] and the result lies in [mi, ma]. If ma == mi - 1 the divisor is 0 (division by zero); if ma < mi - 1 the divisor wraps to a large unsigned value and the result is not confined to a meaningful range. No locks or memory are touched beyond the arc4random call.
contract: /*@ requires mi <= ma && ma - mi < 2147483647; ensures result >= mi && result <= ma; */
note: tools/test/stress2/lib/random_int.c:32-36 (one-line body at 35). Reviewer round 15 is right (arc4random is unsigned, modulo non-negative); the earlier prose claim of a negative remainder was wrong. Reviewer round 1 (range [mi,ma]) is right.

name: test
prose: Creates a Unix stream socket pair in the static sv; if socketpair fails it calls err(1) and the process exits. It then forks. In the child (fork returned 0) it runs writer(), which allocates bufsize bytes (err(1) in the child if malloc fails), fills them with ascending ints and writes them to sv[1] in a loop until a write fails; a write failing with EPIPE makes writer return and the child calls _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS), any other write failure calls err(1) in the child only. In the parent (pid > 0) it runs reader(), which allocates bufsize bytes (err(1) in the parent on malloc failure), reads from sv[0] until read returns 0 or done_testing becomes nonzero (err(1) in the parent if read returns a negative value), then closes sv[0]; the parent then sends SIGINT to the child and returns 0, without waiting for the child or closing sv[1]. If fork fails it calls err(1). bufsize is set by setup() (static, zero before setup runs).
note: tools/test/stress2/testcases/socket/socket.c:98-116, reader 48-61, writer 63-83. Reviewer round 15 right (child malloc/write failure exits only the child; parent returns 0); round 2 right (read runs in the parent, parent malloc failure also exits). setup at 85-91 sets bufsize = 2 << random_int(2,12).

name: main
prose: Entry point of indent_wrapper (the name process_diff does not exist in the file; the slice is the tail of main). It installs a SIGPIPE handler, parses options with getopt (-v verbosity, -t diff tool, -g/-d/-D/-s/-c choose the command whose output is the diff; any other option calls usage()), and calls usage() if no command was selected. It runs that command into a block list, splits the diff into a pre-image list diff_a_head and a post-image list diff_b_head, and then makes passes over diff_a_head: (1) any non-printable ASCII byte other than tab, CR, LF and space makes errx(EX_SOFTWARE) end the process, bytes with the high bit get the BLOCK_MASK flag; (2) comments and (3) preprocessor lines and strings are masked; (4) text inside braces or parentheses is masked, and unbalanced nesting or an unterminated string ends the process via errx(EX_SOFTWARE); (6) for each run of lines carrying the added flag that is not masked, it copies the run into indent_in_head, pipes it through the fixed indent and sed command line via cmd_block_process into indent_out_head, compares the two with diff_tool (when -t was given) or diff_block, sets retval to 1 if the comparison reports a difference, and frees both temporary lists. It returns retval (0 initially, 1 if any region differed). The diff lists, the command buffer and the diff_head list are not freed. Details of the head (lines 368-436) and the diff-splitting loop (436-526) were read only in outline.
note: tools/tools/indent_wrapper/indent_wrapper.c:368-744 (main); passes at 527-668, sixth pass 669-743, return at 743. Real function is main; process_diff does not exist (grep). Partly read: the diff splitting loop 436-526 and the second/third pass bodies 539-608 were only skimmed.

name: main
prose: Entry point of kttcp (slice cut the head; whole function is kttcp.c:102-306). Options are parsed with getopt: -4/-6 (a second family option calls usage()), -b (buffer size, errx(1) if above INT_MAX), -n, -p, -q, -r/-t (a second direction option calls usage()), -v; -w is in the getopt string but has no case so it falls into usage(), as does any unknown option. usage() is called if neither -r nor -t was given, and in send mode if no host argument follows. It opens the kttcp device, resolves the address with getaddrinfo, creates a stream socket from the first usable address, then either (send) connects and sets SO_SNDBUF or (receive) sets SO_REUSEADDR, binds, listens, accepts one connection and sets SO_RCVBUF on it; failures of open, getaddrinfo, socket, connect, setsockopt, bind, listen, accept and the kttcp ioctl exit with err/errx status 2. It takes rusage before and after the ioctl (their return values are not checked), prints byte and bit rates, a CPU-time line when verbose > 1 and a user/sys/real line, then closes the kttcp socket, the listening socket in receive mode and the device (close results unchecked), calls freeaddrinfo and returns 0. The code divides by the kernel-reported elapsed microseconds and, with -v, by the CPU time delta, without checking for zero.
note: tools/tools/kttcp/kttcp.c:102-306; ioctl 258-259, division by usecs 265, by CPU time 272-273, closes 299-302. Reviewer claim (any system-call failure exits) is right: getrusage and close results are ignored; prose now lists which failures exit. Partly read: option parsing and get_bytes helper skimmed.

name: handle_rtmsg
prose: Handles one routing message; msglen is unused. If rtm_version differs from RTM_VERSION it logs an error and returns. For RTM_IFANNOUNCE it logs an arrival (debug) or a departure and, on departure, calls wds_destroy with the announced interface name; other announce kinds do nothing. For RTM_IEEE80211 it switches on the event kind: DISASSOC is ignored unless discover_on_join is set and then falls into LEAVE; LEAVE, if checkifnet(ifan_name, 1) is true, logs 'station leave' and calls wds_leave with the event address, otherwise does nothing; JOIN, REJOIN, ASSOC and REASSOC are ignored unless discover_on_join is set and then fall into WDS; WDS logs '[addr] wds discovery' unconditionally, then, only if checkifnet succeeds, calls wds_discovery with the interface name and address. Other event kinds and other message types are ignored. It returns nothing; the wds list is changed only through wds_destroy, wds_leave and wds_discovery.
note: tools/tools/net80211/wlanwds/wlanwds.c:392-455 (version check 398-402, IFANNOUNCE 404-420, IEEE80211 421-452). Reviewer round 15 is right: the 'wds discovery' log at 444 precedes the checkifnet test at 446 (prose fixed); reviewer 1 (version-mismatch return) is right and is stated

name: update_ip6
prose: Copies the IPv6 and UDP headers out of pkt, steps the source then possibly destination address/port fields inside a single-pass do-while(0), adjusts the UDP checksum and copies both headers back into pkt. Source stage: one 16-bit group of the source address (index g->src_ip.ipv6.sgroup) and the UDP source port. With OPT_RANDOM_SRC both are replaced with nrand48 values and the stage ends (the destination is not touched). Otherwise, if the source port is below src_ip.port1 it is incremented and the stage ends with the address unchanged; if not, the port is reset to port0 and, if the address group is below the configured end group value, the group is incremented and the stage ends; otherwise the group is reset to the start value and the destination stage runs. In that case the source delta (address and/or port, when they changed) is first accumulated into udp_sum. Destination stage (egroup and UDP destination port): with OPT_RANDOM_DST both get nrand48 values; else the port is incremented if below dst_ip.port1, else reset to port0 and the group incremented if below its end value, else reset to its start value. After the loop the delta of the last stage reached (destination if the destination stage ran, source otherwise) is added to udp_sum, so when the destination stage runs the checksum delta covers both source and destination changes; if udp_sum is nonzero the UDP checksum is adjusted by it. No return value.
note: tools/tools/netmap/pkt-gen.c:914-997 (source stage 927-952, destination 961-984, checksum 986-994). Reviewer round 1 right (OPT_RANDOM_SRC breaks before the destination at 937); reviewer round 15 right (source delta accumulated at 954-959 plus destination delta at 987-992 when both wrap). Old prose said the delta covered 'the last changed pair only' and that the group is advanced by one on every call; both wrong.

name: main
prose: Entry point of syscall_timing (slice cut the head; function is syscall_timing.c:1017-1167). It parses -i iterations (>=1), -l loops (1..100000), -p path, -s alarm seconds (1..3600); a bad number, an unknown option, no test name, or a test name not found in tests[] calls usage(). alarm_timeout starts at 1, so the 'iterations < 1 && alarm_timeout < 1' check at 1068 cannot trigger; if -i is not given iterations becomes UINT64_MAX (bounded by the alarm). In the validation loop, for each named test with FLAG_PATH when -p was not given it does strdup, mkdtemp and asprintf (err(1) on failure), overwriting tmp_dir/tmp_path each time, so with several such tests only the last temporary directory is remembered. It asserts clock_getres succeeds, prints the clock resolution and header, then for each named test: if tmp_path is set it opens/creates it, ftruncate to 1000000 and closes it (err(1) on failure) and uses it as the path for that and every later test; it runs the test once as warmup, then loops times, printing the elapsed time, call count and per-call nanoseconds (divides by the returned call count without checking for zero). At the end, if tmp_path is set it unlinks that file (warning on failure other than ENOENT) and rmdir's the last tmp_dir (warning on failure), and returns 0; earlier temporary directories from the validation loop are not removed.
note: tools/tools/syscall_timing/syscall_timing.c:1017-1167 (validation 1082-1101, run loop 1109-1155, cleanup 1157-1164). Reviewer round 15 right (tmp_dir/tmp_path overwritten at 1094-1097, only last removed); reviewer round 17 wrong: alarm_timeout is initialised to 1 at 1028 so -i or -s is not required (1068-1071).

name: vhbarptluns_act
prose: Real name vhbarptluns_act (static, vhba_rptluns.c:117-364; slice cut the head). Zeroes csio->sense_data, then handles one SCSI command and queues the CCB on vhbas->vhba->done by TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL on every return path (the early returns at 134-135, 146-147, 167-168 and the final insert at 363); each path inserts it once. target_id >= MAX_TGT: status CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT, queued, return. LUN is attached if target_lun < MAX_LUN and its bit is set in vhbas->rpbitmap; if it is not attached and the opcode is not INQUIRY, REPORT_LUNS or REQUEST_SENSE, it calls vhba_fill_sense(ILLEGAL_REQUEST, asc 0x25), queues and returns. Switch on cdb[0]: MODE_SENSE/MODE_SENSE_10 with a page code other than format-device, geometry, cache, control or all-pages fills ILLEGAL_REQUEST (asc 0x24) and returns; otherwise it builds mode data in a local 128-byte buffer (block descriptor unless the DBD bit is set, then the requested pages), computes data_len = min(allocation length from the CDB, dxfer_len, built length), copies that many bytes to csio->data_ptr and sets resid = dxfer_len - data_len (the length byte is stored at the end of the built data rather than at the start of the buffer). READ_6/10/12/16 and WRITE_6/10/12/16: if vhba_rwparm returns nonzero it fills ILLEGAL_REQUEST (asc 0x24) and leaves the switch; otherwise a nonzero data_len is copied between data_ptr and vhbas->disk at the computed offset (read when (cdb[0] & 0xf) == 8, else write) with resid = dxfer_len - data_len, and a zero data_len sets resid = dxfer_len. READ_CAPACITY: if any of CDB bytes 2-5 (the LBA field) is nonzero it fills UNIT_ATTENTION sense (asc 0x24) and leaves the switch; otherwise it writes the last block number (0xffffffff when the PMI bit is set or the last block does not fit in 32 bits) and the block size into the first 8 bytes of data_ptr. Any other opcode is handed to vhba_default_cmd. Paths leaving the switch then clear the CAM status bits and set CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR (plus CAM_AUTOSNS_VALID if scsi_status is CHECK CONDITION) when scsi_status is not OK, or set scsi_status OK and CAM_REQ_CMP when it is. vhba_default_cmd and vhba_fill_sense were read only for what they set (fill_sense sets CHECK CONDITION, vhba.c:154-164); vhba_default_cmd was not read.
note: tools/tools/vhba/rptluns/vhba_rptluns.c:117-364; READ_CAPACITY test at 320 checks cdb[2..5] (LBA bytes), reviewer round 17 is right and the old 'reserved bytes' wording is corrected. Partly read: vhba_default_cmd (vhba.c:232) not read.

name: vhba_rwparm
prose: Defined in tools/tools/vhba/vhba.c, not in this file. Decodes the starting block (lba) and block count (cnt) from a READ/WRITE CDB according to cdb[0] (16-byte, 12-byte, 10-byte and 6-byte forms; in the 6-byte form a count of 0 means 256 and only the low 5 bits of byte 1 are used). For any other opcode it returns -1 with *offset and *tl untouched. If lba + cnt is greater than nblks it returns -1 with *offset and *tl untouched (the sum is computed in 64 bits and is not checked for wraparound). Otherwise it stores *tl = cnt << blk_shift (32-bit shift) and *offset = lba << blk_shift and returns 0.
note: tools/tools/vhba/vhba.c:166-230 (returns at 221, 225, 229). The packet marked it 'called, not defined here'; it does exist in vhba.c, so it is fixed rather than dropped.

name: nextjob
prose: Opens ATJOB_DIR ".SEQ" with fopen mode "r+". If that succeeds it scans one value with fscanf("%5lx"): on success it rewinds, sets jobno = (1 + jobno) % 0xfffff (C remainder, so a negative scanned value, which %lx accepts as a signed field of at most 5 characters such as -ffff, gives a negative result), writes it back with fprintf "%05lx\n" (without truncating and without checking the write), closes the file and returns jobno; if the scan does not yield 1 it closes the file and returns EOF (-1) with no write. If the "r+" open fails it tries fopen mode "w" (which truncates an existing file it can open for writing); on success it writes "00001\n", closes the file and returns 1; if that also fails it returns EOF. For a scanned value in 0..0xfffff the returned value is in 0..0xffffe; with a negative scanned value as low as -0xffff it is in -0xfffe..-1 or 0. Return values of fprintf and fclose are not checked, and a legitimate return of -1 cannot be told apart from EOF.
note: usr.bin/at/at.c:180-203 (r+ branch 186-196, create branch 197-201, final EOF 202). Reviewer round 2 (negative hex can give negative return) is right: %5lx accepts a sign; reviewer round 15 (range 0..0xffffe only) is wrong for a signed field, so the prose keeps both ranges

name: main
prose: Entry point of at/atq/atrm/batch (slice cut the head; usr.bin/at/at.c:731-914). It records the real/effective ids with RELINQUISH_PRIVS, takes the basename of argv[0] as the program name and picks the mode from it: atq -> ATQ (options "q:v"), atrm -> ATRM (options ""), batch -> BATCH ("f:q:mv"), anything else AT. getopt then handles: -v (verify), -m (mail), -f (input file), -q (queue; usage() if the argument is longer than one character or not a letter), -r and -d (-d warns, then both: usage() unless the mode is AT, then mode ATRM), -t (usage() unless mode is AT, then timer = ttime(arg)), -l (usage() unless mode AT, then ATQ with options "q:"), -b (usage() unless mode AT, then BATCH), -c (sets mode CAT with no mode check, so it is accepted whatever the current mode is), and any other option calls usage(). If check_permission() fails it calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE). It then runs the selected mode: ATQ reduces privileges to DAEMON_UID/GID, builds a job list from the remaining arguments when no queue was given with -q and calls list_jobs; ATRM reduces privileges to DAEMON_UID/GID and calls process_jobs(..., ATRM); CAT calls process_jobs(..., CAT) without a REDUCE_PRIV call in main; AT takes the time from -t or parsetime(argc, argv), optionally prints it with -v and calls writefile; BATCH upper-cases the queue given with -q or uses DEFAULT_BATCH_QUEUE, uses parsetime if arguments remain or the current time otherwise, optionally prints it, and calls writefile; any other mode value calls panic(). After the handler it calls exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). The callees (list_jobs, process_jobs, writefile, parsetime) can themselves exit. Main does not return.
note: usr.bin/at/at.c:731-914; mode selection 760-771, getopt 776-843, permission 849-850, switch 851-912, exit 913. Reviewer round 15 right (REDUCE_PRIV only in ATQ 854 and ATRM 863, not CAT 870, AT or BATCH); reviewer round 17 right (-c at 836 has no 'program != AT' check). The callees were not read in full.

name: main
prose: Entry point of banner (usr.bin/banner/banner.c:1017-1161, slice cut the head). Options: -d (debug), -t (trace), -w width where atoi(optarg) must be in 1..DWIDTH (else errx(1)); any other option calls usage(), which exits 1. It marks which of the DWIDTH columns are printed for the chosen width. The message is the remaining arguments joined by single spaces in a malloc'd buffer (err(1) if malloc fails), or, if there are no arguments, a MAXMSG buffer read with fgets after printing "Message: " to stderr (empty message on EOF; a trailing newline is removed). With -d it dumps the asc_ptr and data_table arrays. Each message character must be below NCHARS and have a nonzero asc_ptr entry; for each bad one it prints a warning, and if any were bad it calls exit(1). Then for each character it runs a small interpreter over data_table starting at asc_ptr[ch]: bytes >= 128 emit (x & 63) output rows (and end the character when x > 192), other bytes pair as (start, length) of '#' cells on the current row; if the program counter is below 0 or above NBYTES it prints "bad pc" and exit(1). Writes into line[] (x+y) and the print[] index linen are not range-checked against DWIDTH in the code. At the end it frees the message buffer (line 1159) and calls exit(0); it does not return.
note: usr.bin/banner/banner.c:1017-1161; free(message) at 1159. Reviewer round 15 (code never frees the message) is wrong; round 2 (only returns 0 or exits 1) is consistent with the code, which never executes a return; round 1 (argv[argc]==NULL) is only a C-runtime fact and not asserted in the prose.

name: sppd_write
prose: Writes buffer to fd in a loop while size > 0. A write returning -1 with errno other than EINTR makes the function return -1 immediately (bytes already written are not reported); -1 with EINTR and a 0 return are both retried, so a write that keeps returning 0 makes the loop spin without progress. A positive write result advances the buffer pointer, reduces size and adds to the running count. When size reaches 0 it returns the number of bytes written, which equals the original size when the original size was positive, and 0 when the original size was 0 or negative (no write is made). The caller must supply at least size readable bytes at buffer (the buffer is only read). It acquires no locks and allocates no memory.
note: usr.bin/bluetooth/rfcomm_sppd/rfcomm_sppd.c:410-436 (return -1 at 420, return wrote at 435). Reviewer round 15 right (buffer is the source, so readable not writable); round 1 right (only -1 or the full size).

name: zwrite
prose: Write callback of the compress stream (usr.bin/compress/zopen.c:231-317; slice cut the head). If num == 0 it returns 0 at once (line 241) without touching the state. Otherwise, if the state is not yet S_MIDDLE (first call) it sets the state to S_MIDDLE before doing anything else, writes the 3-byte magic header (magic bytes then maxbits|block_compress) with fwrite and returns -1 if either fwrite is short, then initialises the output/hash state, takes the first input byte *bp as the current prefix code and clears the hash table. A later call goes straight to the 'middle' label. The loop consumes the remaining input bytes, looking each up in the hash table (primary then secondary probing); a miss calls output() for the current prefix (return -1 on failure), adds a table entry while free_ent < maxmaxcode, else, once in_count reaches the checkpoint and block compression is on, calls cl_block() (return -1 on failure). It returns num when all bytes were consumed. After a -1 return the already-consumed input is not rolled back; because the state was set to S_MIDDLE before the header was written, a failed header write leaves a later call skipping header and initialisation, so the state is not safe to retry. It allocates no memory.
note: usr.bin/compress/zopen.c:231-317 (num==0 return 241-242, state set 247-249, header 252-257, loop 280-315, return 316). Reviewer round 15 is half right: there is a num==0 early return (prose keeps it, contrary to the reviewer), but the header write and *bp read happen and a failed header/output leaves the state not retryable (prose corrected). output()/cl_block() were not read in full.

name: PF_funcs
prose: Scans the global input stream inf for Fortran/Pascal-style declarations (usr.bin/ctags/fortran.c:44-126). It loops, storing ftell(inf) in lineftell, reading a line into lbuf with fgets and returning pfcnt (true if at least one declaration reached pfnote, else false) as soon as fgets returns NULL (end of file or error); there is no other return. Per line: lineno is incremented, lbp points at lbuf, an initial '%' and following whitespace are skipped, and an empty remainder skips the line. An optional type keyword is matched case-insensitively by cicmp (complex, character, integer, logical, real, each followed by takeprec which consumes an optional '*' and digits; or 'double', then whitespace, which must be followed by 'precision' or the line is skipped, and for double precision takeprec is not called). The type keyword is optional: a line starting with function, program, procedure or subroutine is accepted without one, and no whitespace is required after the keyword match. After the keyword (function, program or procedure, or subroutine) and whitespace, a name must follow whose first character is accepted unchecked and whose remaining characters are consumed while intoken() holds; a one-character name is rejected (line skipped). The name is cut with EOS in lbuf, copied with strlcpy into tok (truncated to the buffer size), then get_line() and pfnote(tok, lineno) are called and pfcnt is set. It holds no locks and allocates nothing. get_line, pfnote, intoken were not read.
note: usr.bin/ctags/fortran.c:44-126; type switch 63-91, keyword switch 96-110, token 111-123; cicmp 132-146, takeprec 148-162. Reviewer round 2 right (type keyword optional, one-char identifiers rejected); round 15 right ('double precision' path at 69-76 never calls takeprec); formal contract rejected earlier is not retained (empty)

name: main
prose: Entry point of ctlstat (usr.bin/ctlstat/ctlstat.c:846-1007; slice cut the head). Defaults: waittime 1, count -1, 3 devices, CPU and header shown. It reads sysctl kern.cam.ctl.max_luns into ctl_stat_bits (1024 if the sysctl fails), allocates the item bitmask with bit_alloc (err(1) on failure), and parses options. -c sets count and -w the wait time with atoi (no validation); -l and -p add one LUN or port to the mask, with errx(1) only if the number is greater than ctl_stat_bits (negative values and a value equal to ctl_stat_bits are not rejected here) ; -n sets the device count; -P selects Prometheus mode; the default (unknown option) branch calls usage(1) and exit(1). After parsing: -l together with -p is errx(1); in Prometheus mode, if count != -1, waittime != 1, ports were requested or totals were requested, it calls errx(1), otherwise sets count to 1 (so -c 1 or -w 1 passed explicitly are not detected). If neither LUNs nor ports were selected it selects ports when totals are on, else LUNs. It opens CTL_DEFAULT_DEV (err(1) on failure), prints an HTTP/1.1 200 header in Prometheus mode, then loops while count != 0: in Prometheus mode it calls get_and_print_stats twice (LUNs then ports), otherwise once with the ports flag from the context; it prints a blank line, flushes, clears the first-run flag, sleeps waittime unless count == 1, and decrements count if it is positive. A negative count (the default) loops forever; count 0 skips the loop. After the loop it calls exit(retval), which is 0 unless the usage branch set it; get_and_print_stats (not read) can itself terminate the process. The fd is not closed explicitly.

name: main
prose: Entry point of diff (usr.bin/diff/diff.c:138-483; slice cut the head). It parses the option letters and long options into globals; options that conflict with an already chosen output format call conflicting_format(), invalid arguments (for example --tabsize or --color values, the context count) call usage() after a warning, -X calls read_excludes_file (which exits 2 through err if the file cannot be opened), --version prints diff_version and exit(0), and several branches call usage(). It defaults the format to D_NORMAL (D_CONTEXT if the prototype flag is set and no format chose), sets colour codes when do_color() and DIFFCOLORS is present, and (OpenBSD builds only) calls pledge. If the operand count is not 2 it calls usage(). It compiles the ignore and most-recent patterns with checked_regcomp (errx(2) on failure), stats or fstats the two operands ('-' means stdin); a failing stat is err(2) unless -N was given and errno is ENOENT, in which case that side is treated as empty; if both are empty it warns and exit(2). Comparing stdin to a directory is errx(2). If both operands are directories it errors out with status 2 when -D is in use, else calls diffdir; otherwise a directory operand is replaced by splice(dir, other) and re-stat'd (err(2) on failure) and diffreg is called and reported through print_status. It then flushes stdout (err(2) if that fails) and calls exit(status) with the global status accumulated by the comparison routines (0 when no differences were reported, 1 when differences were found, 2 when errors were recorded). It does not return. Usage() and the callees were not read in full.
note: usr.bin/diff/diff.c:138-483; read_excludes_file 524-547 (err(2) at 535), exit(0) version 383-384, comparison 425-482. Reviewer round 15 right: unopenable -X file exits 2 (added). Partly read: option cases 158-330 skimmed, usage(), diffdir, diffreg, print_status not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of dpv (usr.bin/dpv/dpv.c:250-476; slice cut the head). It records argv[0], mallocs and zeroes a dpv_config (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if out of memory) and parses options. -a, -p, -b and -t copy their argument into malloc'd storage (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) on malloc failure); -D and -X choose the display type; -d sets debug; -h and any unknown option call usage(); -i/-I set status formats (later overwritten, see below); -k keeps the tite; -l selects line mode; -m multiple-file mode; -N, -T, -w set option bits; -o and -x set the output file or shell command; -L, -n, -P and -U take strtol(optarg, NULL, 10) results (a negative -L/-P below -1 becomes -1, a negative -n becomes -1), and the check 'value == 0 && errno == EINVAL' calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE) only if errno was already EINVAL, because strtol does not set EINVAL for a non-numeric string; such an argument normally just yields 0. The remaining arguments are turned into a linked list of file nodes (malloc and zero each, errx on failure): a leading 'number:' is parsed with sscanf into the node's length and stripped from the name, otherwise the length is -1; with -m each label must be followed by a path argument (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if missing), without -m only the first argument is used and the loop stops after one node. If no label was given it warns and calls usage(). With the default libdialog display it installs sig_int for SIGINT (the sigaction struct's mask and flags are not initialised). The status line formats are then set unconditionally for line or byte mode (overwriting -i and -I) together with the action callback. It calls dpv(config, file_list), warns only if that returns nonzero and -d was given, calls end_dialog() unless -k was given, calls dpv_free() and exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). usage() (490-543) exits with EXIT_FAILURE, printing the text only when debug is off. Main does not return; the config and file nodes are not freed here.

Reviewer round 15 is right: strtol does not set EINVAL for non-numeric input so errx is not reached by that route (prose corrected). The called libraries (dpv, end_dialog, dpv_free) were not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of elfdump (usr.bin/elfdump/elfdump.c:504-708; slice cut the head). Options set bits in flags (-a sets flags = ED_ALL and -E sets flags = ED_IS_ELF, both replacing earlier bits; the others OR in a single bit); -w opens the named file for writing as the output stream (err(1) if it cannot be opened or its rights cannot be limited to CAP_FSTAT and CAP_WRITE); an unknown option calls usage(). usage() is also called if no operand remains, if no flag was set, or if -E is combined with more than one operand, other flags or -w; extra operands beyond the first are otherwise ignored (only *av is used). It opens the first operand read-only and fstat's it (err(1) on failure; the descriptor is not closed later); a file smaller than an Elf32_Ehdr exits 1 (silently with -E, errx 'not an elf file' otherwise). It limits rights (CAP_MMAP_R on the file, none on stdin, stdout/stderr limits) and enters capability mode, each failure being err(1), then maps the whole file read-only with MAP_SHARED (err(1) on MAP_FAILED). If the magic check fails it exits 1 (errx otherwise); with -E on a valid ELF it exit(0)s without printing. Otherwise it reads header offsets and counts from the mapped image, locates the section header string table and the .strtab and .dynstr section data (offsets and indices taken from the file are not checked against the file size), prints the ELF header, program headers and section headers if requested, walks the program headers (printing the interpreter if requested) and the section headers dispatching to the print routines by section type under the corresponding flag bits, and returns 0. The mapping is never unmapped. Because it never returns nonzero, all error exits are exit/err/errx/usage calls. The print routines were not read.
note: usr.bin/elfdump/elfdump.c:504-708; option parsing 529-577, usage check 580-582, size check 586-590, ELF check 604-609, return 707. Reviewer round 15 right: only ac == 0 is checked for non -E use (prose now says extra operands are ignored, and the -E case requires exactly one). The print_* helpers were not read.

name: do_printf
prose: Real name do_printf (usr.bin/find/printf.c:159-348; the packet name was truncated and the slice cut the head). It runs plan->c_data through escape(), which may set a flush request and a warned flag (F_HAS_WARNED is set on the plan if warned), and then walks the escaped string. Ordinary characters are copied to fout with putc. After '%', the next character selects the field: the literal percent, path (%p), file name (%f), directory part of the path or '.' if there is no '/' (%h), group and user names or numbers (%g %G %u %U), octal mode (%m), ls-style mode (%M), blocks and sizes (%k %b %s %S, %S printing blocks*512/size as a float), depth (%d), device (%D), link target (%l, printing nothing if readlink returns 0 or fails), inode, link count, file type (%y; %Y follows a symlink with stat and prints L, N or ? when stat fails with the loop, missing or other errors), and the access, change, modification time forms (%a %c %t with ctime, %A %C %T taking the next format character for strftime, %B likewise for birth time but printing nothing when st_birthtime is 0 or the system lacks it); %Z prints nothing. %P, %H and %F, the numeric modifier characters and '.', and any unknown character call errx(1, ...) without returning (the escaped buffer is then not freed). At the end it fflush(fout) if the flush flag was set, frees the escaped copy and returns nothing. The format-taking cases (%A, %B, %C, %T) consume the next format character even if it is the terminating NUL, after which the loop reads past the end of the string. escape(), fp_ctime and fp_strftime were not read in full.
note: usr.bin/find/printf.c:159-348; %B at 315-321 (birthtime test 317), errx cases 204-207, 246-247, 336-342, flush/free 345-347. Reviewer round 17 right (%B prints nothing if birthtime is zero); the old prose said every specifier prints from the entry. Real function is do_printf, not print_stat_format.

name: print_pts_info
prose: Static function (usr.bin/fstat/fstat.c:498-517) taking a procstat handle and a filestat. It calls procstat_get_pts_info into local pts and errbuf variables (not caller storage). If that returns nonzero it prints "* error" (no newline) and returns. Otherwise it prints "* pseudo-terminal master ", then, when the -n flag (nflg) is set or pts.devname is the empty string, the device number pts.dev as %#10jx, else pts.devname as %10s, and finally calls print_access_flags(fst->fs_fflags). Its only effect is output on stdout; it keeps no pointer to its locals.
note: usr.bin/fstat/fstat.c:498-517; the error return at 506-509, device print 511-515. Reviewer round 15 right (pts and errbuf are locals); prose corrected. procstat_get_pts_info and print_access_flags were not read.

name: MCParse
prose: Reads the catalog source from fd line by line with get_line until it returns NULL, then returns (no value). Lines starting with '$': '$set N' calls MCAddSet(atoi) and resets msgid to 0; '$delset N' calls MCDelSet(atoi); '$quote' sets the local quote character to the first non-blank character after it, or to 0 if there is none (this is local state only, nothing is added to the catalog); a '$' followed by whitespace is ignored; any other '$' line gives an 'unrecognized line' warning if text remains. Other lines: an empty line is skipped; a line not starting with a digit gets a warning and is skipped; otherwise msgid = atoi, the id digits and following blanks are skipped, and if nothing remains MCDelMsg(msgid) is called, else getmsg(fd, text, quote) builds the message (backslash escapes, an optional leading quote character, a closing quote character ending the text when followed only by whitespace to the end of the line, otherwise warned about and kept) and MCAddMsg(msgid, str) is called. An unterminated quote simply ends at the end of that line, with no error. getmsg calls error() (which terminates the program) if a trailing backslash is followed by end of file; the callees MCAddSet, MCDelSet, MCAddMsg, MCDelMsg and get_line can also terminate the program via error(), which was not read here. getmsg's message buffer is static and reused between calls.
note: usr.bin/gencat/gencat.c:395-469 (loop 403-468); getmsg 307-392 (premature end of file error at 343-345). Reviewer round 1/2 right (unterminated quote ends at end of line); reviewer round 15 right ($quote handled at 417-427 only sets the local variable). MCAddSet/MCDelSet/MCAddMsg/MCDelMsg/get_line not read.

name: procmatch_match
prose: Static helper (usr.bin/grep/util.c:203-244) called for a matching line. First, independently of mc->printmatch: if mc->doctx is set, it prints "--\n" when first_match is false and either mc->same_file is false or mc->last_outed > 0, calls printqueue() when Bflag > 0, and sets mc->tail = Aflag. Then, if mc->printmatch is set, it calls printline(pc, ':', &last_out); while pc->matchidx >= MAX_MATCHES it resets matchidx to 0, re-runs procline(pc) and calls printline again if that returned !vflag, otherwise leaves the loop; if the last printline did not terminate the line it calls printline once more; finally it sets first_match = false, mc->same_file = true and mc->last_outed = 0. If printmatch is not set, none of the printing or the first_match / same_file / last_outed updates happen, but the doctx separator, queue flush and tail update still do when doctx is set. No return value.
note: usr.bin/grep/util.c:203-244 (doctx block 207-213, printmatch block 216-243). Reviewer round 15 right: the doctx block runs regardless of printmatch (old prose said nothing updated); round 1 reviewer's complaint (state updated only if printmatch) is right for first_match/same_file/last_outed. printline/procline/printqueue not read.

name: litexec
prose: Literal-string matcher (usr.bin/grep/util.c:437-487, compiled only with WITH_INTERNAL_NOSPEC). It uses strcasestr when cflags has REG_ICASE, else strstr. The search region is taken from pmatch[0]: ofs = rm_so, stringlen = rm_eo. If ofs >= stringlen it returns REG_NOMATCH without touching pmatch. It copies the first stringlen bytes of string with strndup (so the copy stops at an embedded NUL) and returns REG_ESPACE if that fails. The loop stops when pat->len exceeds the remaining text, when no occurrence is found, or, when nmatch == 0, after the first occurrence (pmatch is not written in that case). When nmatch > 0 each occurrence is recorded in pmatch[idx] as absolute offsets (rm_so = ofs + offset, rm_eo = rm_so + pat->len) and idx is incremented; the loop ends when idx reaches nmatch; otherwise the next search start is computed as pmatch[idx].rm_so + 1 after idx was incremented, i.e. from the entry that has not been written yet (its prior content), not from the match just found, so searching for further occurrences uses whatever the caller left in that entry. The copy is freed on every path after allocation. If at least one occurrence was found and nmatch > 0, the unused entries pmatch[idx..nmatch-1] are set to -1/-1. It returns 0 if at least one occurrence was counted, else REG_NOMATCH.
note: usr.bin/grep/util.c:437-487; ofs update at 476 reads pmatch[idx] after the ++idx at 474. Reviewer round 15 is right (uses the not-yet-written entry); the earlier prose ('stores the absolute offsets of the found occurrences') overstated correctness of later matches. Early returns at 454 and 457 leave pmatch untouched; free at 481.

name: printline
prose: Real name printline (usr.bin/grep/util.c:774-856; slice cut the head). It starts with a = *last_out and terminated = true. If oflag and matchall are both set it returns true immediately, without printing, without writing *last_out and without incrementing pc->printed. If (oflag || color) and (pc->printed > 0 || pc->matchidx > 0): with color and not -o it prints the line metadata once when nothing was printed yet; for each of the first matchidx matches that is not zero-length it (with -o) sets pc->ln.boff to the match start and prints the metadata, or (without -o) writes the text from a up to the match start; wraps the match text in color escapes when color is set, sets a to the match end, and with -o writes a newline. Then it stores a in *last_out (which equals the old *last_out if no non-empty match was processed, so its value is unchanged in that case). Without -o and when matchidx != MAX_MATCHES it writes the remaining tail (and sets *last_out = ln.len) if any, then a newline and fflush; without -o and with matchidx == MAX_MATCHES it prints no newline and sets terminated = false; with -o it just fflushes. In the other case (neither -o nor color, or no match and nothing printed yet) it calls grep_printline(&pc->ln, sep). In every non-early path it then increments pc->printed and returns terminated, which is false only for the no -o / MAX_MATCHES case above. It also modifies pc->ln.boff in the -o case.
note: usr.bin/grep/util.c:774-856 (early return 789-790, match branch 795-851, grep_printline 853, printed++ 854). Reviewer round 15 is mixed: *last_out is assigned at 831 but a starts as *last_out (776), so the value is unchanged when there are no non-empty matches; the prose says so explicitly and mentions the extra boff write. printline_metadata and grep_printline not read.

name: dump_line
prose: Flushes the current label, code and comment buffers to the output stream (usr.bin/indent/io.c:60-221). First, if ps.procname is non-empty it clears it and sets ps.ind_level to 0. If all three buffers are empty it either decrements suppress_blanklines when that is positive or sets ps.bl_line and increments n_real_blanklines, and prints nothing. Otherwise, if inhibit_formatting is false it clears suppress_blanklines and ps.bl_line, adjusts the pending blank-line count and prints it, counts a code line when a label or code is present, and prints: the label (first closing an open comment with a ".*/" line, trimming trailing blanks, padding, and handling #else/#endif tails), then the code (closing an open comment first, adjusting ps.paren_indents entries for the paren levels, padding and copying characters, with the 0200 marker expanded to a number), then the comment section if present (placed at ps.com_col plus delta, moved to a new line when the cursor is already past the target, trailing space trimmed; an open comment is not closed by this section), then a newline or form feed and ps.out_lines is incremented. When the line is non-empty but inhibit_formatting is set, nothing is written. On every path (including the empty-line and inhibit_formatting paths) it then sets ps.decl_on_line, ps.ind_stmt, ps.use_ff = false and ps.dumped_decl_indent = 0, empties the three buffers (the comment buffer restarts at combuf + 1), reloads ps.ind_level and ps.paren_level from ps.i_l_follow and ps.p_l_follow, sets paren_target from ps.paren_indents when ps.paren_level > 0, and sets not_first_line to 1.
note: usr.bin/indent/io.c:60-221; empty test 75-82, formatted branch 83-202, label 108-131, code 137-159, comment 160-189 (comment_open closed only at 109-112 and 140-143), tail 203-220. Reviewer round 1 right (empty line / inhibit_formatting write nothing); reviewer round 15 right (comment-only line does not close an open comment). compute_code_target and pad_output partly read.

name: parse
prose: Feeds one token code tk to indent's construct parser (usr.bin/indent/parse.c:52-221). First, while the top of ps.p_stack is ifhead and tk is not elselit, it rewrites that entry to stmt and calls reduce() (this happens before the switch, also for a tk that is later rejected). The switch then does: decl pushes one decl entry if the top is not already decl (setting break_comma, ps.il, and with ljust_decl recomputing ps.ind_level and ps.i_l_follow) and sets ps.search_brace; ifstmt (popping an elsehead entry first when 'else if' is enabled), dolit and forstmt push the token, set ps.ind_level and ps.il from ps.i_l_follow and increment ps.i_l_follow; lbrace pushes lbrace and stmt entries and adjusts ps.i_l_follow or ps.ind_level; whilestmt either matches a pending dohead or pushes a while loop entry; elselit turns an ifhead into elsehead, and otherwise only calls diag2(1, "Unmatched 'else'") without changing the stack; rbrace pops back to the matching lbrace and stores stmt, and otherwise (ps.tos == 0 or the entry below the top is not lbrace) only calls diag2(1, "Statement nesting error"); swstmt pushes swstmt and updates case_ind and ps.i_l_follow; semicolon pushes stmt. Any other tk calls diag2(1, "Unknown code to parser") and returns without reaching the checks below. For all other cases, including the two diagnosed ones, control falls out of the switch: if ps.tos >= STACKSIZE - 1 it calls errx(1, "Parser stack overflow"); otherwise reduce() is called, which can still change the stack, and the function returns. The array index ps.tos is not checked before the pushes in the switch, only after.
note: usr.bin/indent/parse.c:52-221; leading loop 60-65, elselit 157-170, rbrace 172-180, default 202-204, overflow 209-210, reduce 212. Reviewer round 15 right (diagnosed else/rbrace still reach reduce(); unknown tk may reduce in the leading loop); round 1 right (errx and default early return). reduce() only partly read.

name: kernel_wait
prose: Polls the iSCSI driver until all sessions are connected (usr.bin/iscsictl/iscsictl.c:553-607). Each poll reallocs the states buffer to nentries entries (xo_err(1) and exit on realloc failure) and issues the ISCSISLIST ioctl on iscsi_fd; if it fails with EMSGSIZE, nentries is multiplied by 4 and the call is repeated; any other failure prints a warning via xo_warn and returns the ioctl's nonzero result (the ioctl failure value, -1). On success it scans the isl_nentries entries returned and returns 0 if every one has iss_connected set (also 0 when the list is empty). Otherwise it sleeps one second; if timeout > 0 it decrements it and returns 1 when it reaches 0 (so a positive timeout allows that many polls); a timeout of 0 or below never reaches that test and polls forever. The states buffer is not freed on any return path. The function has no formal contract because it works through a file descriptor and ioctl.
note: usr.bin/iscsictl/iscsictl.c:553-607 (EMSGSIZE retry 574-578, error return 581-584, all_connected return 596-597, timeout 601-605). Reviewer original (timeout=0 means infinite) is right and the prose states it; the empty contract is kept because of the ioctl/errno dependency (the earlier contract was not meaningful)

name: yyparse
prose: Generated byacc LALR parser for the lex input grammar (usr.bin/lex/initparse.c:719-1843; the head is the YYPARSE_DECL() definition, here yyparse(void)). It resets yynerrs, yyerrflag, yychar (to YYEMPTY) and the state, allocates the initial stack through yygrowstack if none exists (a failure goes to yyoverflow), then loops: it takes the default reduction for the state if there is one, else reads a token with YYLEX when yychar < 0 (a negative value becomes YYEOF), shifts it (growing the stack when full; growth failure goes to yyoverflow) or reduces by the grammar rule; the rule actions (lines 845-1810, which run the semantic code for the lex grammar) were not read. On a syntax error it calls YYERROR_CALL("syntax error") (unless already recovering), increments yynerrs (also for the YYERROR action), and tries to pop states to one that accepts the error token, with yyerrflag = 3; if the stack is exhausted or the next token is YYEOF during recovery it goes to yyabort. On yyoverflow it calls YYERROR_CALL("yacc stack overflow") and falls through into yyabort (so the function does not return 2). Both yyabort and yyaccept call yyfreestack (freeing the state and value stacks) before returning: yyabort returns 1 and yyaccept (reached by a reduction in the final state when yychar is YYEOF) returns 0. The stack is therefore freed on every return, and the caller must not free it. yygrowstack (665-702) returns YYENOMEM only to its caller within yyparse.
note: usr.bin/lex/initparse.c:719-1843; returns 1838 and 1842, yyoverflow 1833-1834 falling into yyabort, yyerrlab 794-796, recovery 797-842. The old prose (returns 2 on stack growth failure; stack storage kept by caller) was wrong; reviewer round 15 (side effects omitted) right. Partly read: rule actions 845-1810 not read, so semantic-action effects are not described.

name: YY_DECL
prose: Generated function flexscan (YY_DECL at initscan.c:1914-1915 expands to 'int flexscan(void)'; the function body runs from line 2191 to 4282; the packet called it yylex, which does not exist here). It is the flex scanner for flex's own input. On its first call it sets yy_init, the start state, yyin/yyout to stdin/stdout when unset and creates the first buffer. It then loops, matching the longest rule with the DFA tables, backing up to the last accepting state if needed, and runs the selected rule action. Rule actions return a token code (for example '<', '^', '"', '$', '\n', BEGIN_REPEAT_POSIX or BEGIN_REPEAT_FLEX, EOF_OP, as in rules 139-151) or just update scanner state (linenum, sectnum, bracelevel, start conditions via BEGIN, output via ACTION_ECHO) and continue the loop. yyterminate() (return 0 / YY_NULL) is used at the end-of-file action of SECT2PROLOG (after mark_prolog and sectnum = 0, line 3156), by rule 152 (the %% line that starts section 3, which sets sectnum = 3, selects SECT3 or SECT3_NOESCAPE and writes a comment, line 3340), and at other EOF actions (lines 2623, 4042, 4051), so it also returns 0 at a section boundary, not only at real end of input. Rule 153 reports 'Input line too long' via synerr and calls FLEX_EXIT(EXIT_FAILURE) when the matched text is not shorter than MAXLINE. Only this slice (rules 130-153), the entry code and the DFA matching loop were read; the other rules and the buffer-refill code were not read, so other return values and exits are not enumerated.
note: usr.bin/lex/initscan.c:1914-1915 (YY_DECL define), 2191-2282 (head and matching loop), slice 3102-3359 (case 130-153; yyterminate at 3156 and 3340; Input line too long exit at 3350-3356). Reviewer round 17 right: yyterminate returns 0 on the section-3 marker rule (case 152) as well as end of input. Partly read: rules outside 130-153 and EOF/refill code were not read.

name: end_order
prose: Closes the current collation order entry (usr.bin/localedef/collate.c:605-693). It saves pri = nextpri and switches on currorder. T_CHAR: for each of the NUM_WT weights it resets order_weights[i] to -1 after setting currchar->ref[i] either to pri with RESOLVED (when the weight was negative, get_pri(ref) is NULL, or the referenced priority is -1) or to the given ref with REFER; then ellipsis_start = currchar->wc + 1 and currchar = NULL. T_ELLIPSIS: copies order_weights into ellipsis_weights and resets order_weights to -1; nothing is resolved. T_COLLELEM: if currelem is NULL it prints an internal fault message (INTERR only prints, it does not exit) and sets no weights; otherwise the same RESOLVED/REFER logic is applied to currelem->ref[i]. T_UNDEFINED: the same logic but an unspecified weight sets pri_undefined[i] to -1 with RESOLVED (not to nextpri). T_SYMBOL: the same logic applied to currundef->ref[i] (currundef is dereferenced without a NULL check). Any other currorder value prints the internal fault message and sets nothing. After the switch nextpri is incremented by one on every path (the INTERR cases do not return early).
note: usr.bin/localedef/collate.c:605-693 (T_CHAR 617-633, T_ELLIPSIS 635-641, T_COLLELEM 643-660, T_UNDEFINED 662-673 with -1 at 667, T_SYMBOL 675-686, default 688-689, nextpri++ 692); INTERR at localedef.h:192 only fprintf. Reviewer round 1 right (T_ELLIPSIS does not resolve); round 15 right (undefined uses -1, not nextpri).

name: start_order_symbol
prose: Calls get_collundef(name) and stores the result in currundef, then calls start_order(T_SYMBOL). get_collundef (collate.c:549-570) looks name up in the collundefs tree; if it is absent it callocs an entry, strdups the name, gives each of NUM_WT refs a new priority and inserts it, and if calloc or strdup fails it prints 'out of memory', frees the entry and returns NULL (currundef is then NULL and add_charmap_undefined is not called); in all non-failing cases (new or existing entry) it then calls add_charmap_undefined(name), which either frees name or records it in the charmap as an undefined symbol (with a warning), so the caller's name must not be used afterwards. start_order sets lastorder to the old currorder, currorder to T_SYMBOL, prints 'character value expected' if the old currorder was T_ELLIPSIS, resets all COLL_WEIGHTS_MAX order_weights to -1 and sets curr_weight to 0.
note: usr.bin/localedef/collate.c:721-725, get_collundef 549-570 (OOM return 561, add_charmap_undefined 568), start_order 695-712; charmap.c:297-311 add_charmap_undefined frees sym in else branch. Reviewer round 1 right (currundef may be NULL); round 15 right (add_charmap_undefined called also for an existing entry).

name: gz_uncompress
prose: Decodes a gzip stream from descriptor in (starting with the prelen bytes in pre, which may be 0) to descriptor out (usr.bin/gzip/gzip.c:718-1055). The comment above says it closes the input, but the code never calls close on in (not at any label), so the caller keeps the descriptor. It allocates two BUFLEN buffers; if malloc fails maybe_err prints (unless -q) and exit(2)s (the later goto labels are reached only through that call, which does not return). It then runs a byte-driven state machine over the header (magic 0, magic 1 (also accepts the old-magic byte), method must be Z_DEFLATED, flags, 6 skipped bytes, optional extra field, original name, comment and header CRC), inflateInit2 with raw deflate, inflate with Z_FINISH writing each output chunk to out unless -t (tflag) is set and updating the CRC and the member length, then checks the trailer CRC and length against the decoded member and loops back to the first magic state for the next member. Read errors, bad magic1, unknown method, inflate errors, write_retry failure, truncated trailer or input, CRC or length mismatch, and a decompression error code all end with out_tot = -1 after a warning. At the start of a member, a first byte that is not the gzip magic byte stops the loop and keeps the count so far, with a 'trailing garbage ignored' warning and exit_value = 2, because in_tot is already greater than 0 at that point whenever any byte has been read or passed in (so even a non-gzip first byte takes this path rather than 'input not gziped (MAGIC0)'); end of input exactly at a member boundary also stops normally. After the loop it calls inflateEnd when the state is past the init state, frees both buffers, stores in_tot (prelen plus all bytes read) in *gsizep if gsizep is non-NULL, and returns out_tot, the total uncompressed bytes counted (0 if no member was decoded) or -1 on failure.
